trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus (€6.75 one-way) or the L9 Sud metro line (€5.15 with T-Casual card) to the city, then connect to Sant Just Desvern via bus L60 or taxi (~€15–18). Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona, freshen up, and take a relaxed evening stroll around the Sant Just Desvern neighbourhood to get your bearings.

meals.dinner: Grab a quick, affordable bite near the hotel – try a local bar or supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) for bocadillos, fruit, and drinks to keep costs low on arrival night. Budget ~€5–8.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a T-Casual 10-trip metro/bus card (€11.35) at the airport – it will save money throughout the trip. The hotel is in Sant Just Desvern, about 8 km southwest of central Barcelona. Keep Day 1 light as you will be tired from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with the crown jewel of Barcelona architecture: the Sagrada Família Guided Tour. Book in advance online to save time and get the best price (~€26–32 with tower access). The guided tour reveals Gaudí's intricate symbolism, the Nativity and Passion facades, and the breathtaking interior forest of columns. Arrive early (opening is 09:00) to beat the summer crowds. Take the metro L5 from Cornellà Centre (near hotel) to Sagrada Família station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to the Eixample district and explore the Manzana de la Discordia (Block of Discord) on Passeig de Gràcia – admire Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside for free. Then stroll up Passeig de Gràcia window-shopping and people-watching. Head to Gràcia neighbourhood for a relaxed afternoon exploring Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia – lively, local, and free.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife. Head to the Eixample 'Gayxample' area or Carrer Blai in El Poble Sec for pre-drinks at budget-friendly bars. Carrer Blai is famous for pintxos bars where you can eat and drink cheaply. Later, explore the bars around Plaça de la Universitat or Carrer Parlament. Clubs don't fill up until after midnight – entry to many is free before 01:00.

meals.breakfast: Café and croissant at a local bar near the hotel or a neighbourhood bakery – budget ~€3–4.
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) near Sagrada Família or Eixample – typically €10–13 for 3 courses including bread and a drink. Look for spots away from the main tourist drag.
meals.dinner: Pintxos crawl on Carrer Blai, El Poble Sec – €1–2 per pintxo, budget ~€10–14 including a beer or two.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets online well in advance – they sell out weeks ahead in August. Wear comfortable shoes; you'll walk 8–10 km today. Stay hydrated – August highs reach ~29°C.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Park Güell (free to enter the monumental zone requires a ticket ~€10, but the surrounding park is free). Arrive early at 08:00 when it opens to avoid the heat and crowds. Marvel at Gaudí's mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and sweeping views over Barcelona. Afterwards, walk downhill through the Gràcia neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Make your way to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) and El Born. Wander the medieval labyrinthine streets for free – visit the Plaça Reial, the Roman ruins visible through the Barcelona History Museum exterior, and the stunning Santa Maria del Mar church (free entry or small donation). Browse the boutiques and street art of El Born. Cool off in the shade of the narrow Gothic lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – a UNESCO World Heritage modernista masterpiece by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Budget tickets start from ~€18–35 depending on the performance. The stained-glass skylight and ornate interior are jaw-dropping, especially illuminated at night. Book in advance at palaumusica.cat. Afterwards, explore the El Born bar scene – try Bar del Convent or nearby craft beer bars.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastry and coffee at a bakery in Gràcia near Park Güell – budget ~€3–5.
meals.lunch: Bocadillo or falafel wrap from a takeaway in the Gothic Quarter – budget ~€4–7. Eat at Plaça de Sant Felip Neri for atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert early dinner at a budget restaurant in El Born or Sant Pere – look for a menú del día or a set dinner menu ~€10–14. Alternatively, grab tapas at a local bar.

day_by_day.notes: Book Park Güell monumental zone tickets online in advance (timed entry slots). The Palau de la Música concert schedule varies – check the website and book as early as possible. Wear smart-casual attire for the concert.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Barceloneta and spend the morning at the beach. Barcelona's urban beaches are free and a quintessential summer experience. Swim, relax, and people-watch. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade and admire Frank Gehry's golden 'Fish' sculpture and the Port Olímpic marina. The beach gets busy by midday so arrive by 09:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Montjuïc hill – take the free escalators from Paral·lel metro station or the Funicular de Montjuïc (included in T-Casual card). Visit the Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic (€3.50) for stunning city views. Walk to the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry) for panoramic views over the city, port, and sea. The Fundació Joan Miró is also here if you want a cultural stop (~€14, but worth it for art lovers).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city for Barcelona's nightlife scene. Head to El Raval neighbourhood – explore Carrer Joaquín Costa and Bar Marsella (one of Barcelona's oldest bars, dating to 1820). Later, check out the clubs around Plaça de Espanya or the beach clubs near Port Olímpic. Many clubs offer free entry with a drink included before 01:00 – look for flyers or apps like Xceed for free guest list entry.

meals.breakfast: Churros con chocolate at a café near Barceloneta – a classic Spanish treat, budget ~€4–6.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood or paella at a budget chiringuito (beach bar) – look for set lunch menus ~€12–15, or grab a bocadillo and eat on the beach for ~€4–6.
meals.dinner: Budget tapas at a bar in El Raval – patatas bravas, pan con tomate, croquetas. Budget ~€10–13 including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Apply sunscreen generously – beach + Montjuïc in August heat is intense. Beware of pickpockets on the beach and in El Raval; keep valuables secure. The Funicular is included in your T-Casual metro card.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau – a stunning UNESCO-listed modernista hospital complex designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner, just a 10-minute walk from Sagrada Família. Entry is ~€16 and far less crowded than other Gaudí sites. The ornate pavilions, gardens, and mosaics are extraordinary. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mercat de Sant Antoni (free to enter) – a beautifully restored 19th-century iron market in Eixample that's a favourite with locals. Browse fresh produce, grab snacks, and soak up the authentic atmosphere. Afterwards, walk through the Eixample grid and spot more modernista architecture: Casa Calvet, Palau del Baró de Quadras, and the ornate pharmacy facades. End with a final stroll down La Rambla (stay alert for pickpockets) and visit La Boqueria market to browse (avoid buying food here – it's overpriced for tourists).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and final night out. Splurge slightly on a sit-down dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant in Eixample or Gràcia – look for Catalan cuisine with a menú de degustació (tasting menu) at budget restaurants (~€20–25). Then head out for one last night of Barcelona nightlife – the clubs in Eixample, Poble Sec, or along the beach at Port Olímpic are all excellent on a Friday night. Many venues are free entry before 01:00 with a drink token.

meals.breakfast: Full Spanish breakfast (tostada con tomate, zumo de naranja, café con leche) at a local bar near the hotel – budget ~€4–6.
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Mercat de Sant Antoni – excellent value at ~€10–13 for a full 3-course meal with wine.
meals.dinner: Farewell Catalan dinner – try escalivada, pa amb tomàquet, fideuà, or crema catalana for dessert. Budget ~€18–25 per person at a mid-range local restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Check out logistics for your departure day if flying home soon – confirm return transport to the airport. Keep €10–15 aside for airport transport. Friday nights in Barcelona are electric – clubs stay open until 05:00–06:00, so pace yourself!

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus or taxi (~25 min) to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll around the local neighbourhood to get oriented. The hotel is near the L3 metro line giving easy access to the city.

meals.breakfast: N/A – on board or at airport
meals.dinner: Light dinner close to the hotel: try Restaurante La Masia de Can Planes in Sant Just Desvern, a welcoming local spot serving Catalan classics like pa amb tomàquet and grilled meats. Budget ~€20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. August evenings are warm (~24°C), so a short walk after dinner is pleasant. Grab a local SIM or activate roaming for navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Take the L3 metro from Zona Universitària (10-min walk from hotel) to Diagonal or Sagrada Família station (~25 min total). Arrive early (9:00–9:30 AM) to beat the August crowds. The guided tour (~90 min) reveals Gaudí's intricate symbolism across the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like nave, and the towers. Book skip-the-line tickets with tower access in advance (~€35–40 pp).
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk – After lunch, head to the Gothic Quarter via metro (L5 to Jaume I). Spend 2–3 hours on a self-guided or small-group walking tour through the medieval labyrinth of Barri Gòtic, the Roman ruins of the Temple d'August, Plaça Reial, and into the trendy El Born neighbourhood. Admire the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and browse the boutiques along Carrer del Rec.
day_by_day.evening: Explore El Born's bar scene for pre-dinner drinks, then enjoy dinner in the neighbourhood. Return to hotel via metro L4 to Passeig de Gràcia then L3 toward Sant Just Desvern.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café – try a croissant and café amb llet at a local bakery (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Bar del Pla in El Born – excellent Catalan tapas, great value lunch menu (menú del día ~€14–16 including wine).
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born – iconic cava bar and tapas spot. Order anchovies, croquetes, and house cava. Budget ~€25–30 pp.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks around 29°C in the afternoon – carry water and wear sunscreen. The Sagrada Família is extremely busy; pre-booked timed entry is essential. Comfortable walking shoes are a must for the Gothic Quarter's cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Pavillon Mies van der Rohe & Montjuïc Architecture Trail – Take the metro L3 to Espanya station (~20 min from hotel area). Visit the Barcelona Pavilion (open from 10:00 AM, ~€12 entry), a serene masterpiece of modernist minimalism with its iconic travertine, glass, and water features. Afterwards, walk up through the Montjuïc gardens, passing the Fundació Joan Miró and the MNAC (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya) for its stunning exterior and city views from the terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Montjuïc circuit: take the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car for panoramic views of the city and port (~€12.70 return). Explore Castell de Montjuïc at the summit. Descend and relax at the Jardins de Laribal, a terraced garden perfect for a mid-afternoon rest in the shade.
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec & Montjuïc Nightlife Circuit – Head down to Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec (10-min walk from Espanya), Barcelona's famous pintxos street. Start with dinner at one of the lively pintxos bars, then move on to Bar Calders or Bodega Sepúlveda for cocktails. Later, head to Sala Apolo or Discothèque Mau Mau for live music or DJ sets – both are Barcelona nightlife institutions in Poble Sec.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia area or grab a bocadillo from a local bakery near the hotel before heading out (~€6–8).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a nearby Mercat or grab a sandwich at the MNAC café with terrace views (~€10–14).
meals.dinner: Pintxos crawl on Carrer de Blai – budget ~€15–20 pp for a full spread of pintxos and a glass of txakoli or local beer.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc is very walkable but hilly – the cable car saves energy for the evening. Poble Sec nightlife starts late (bars fill up after 22:00, clubs after midnight). August nights are warm so light clothing is fine. Check Sala Apolo's programme in advance for live acts.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana Guided Tour or Morning Visit – Take the metro L4 to Urquinaona (~25 min). Arrive at this UNESCO World Heritage modernista masterpiece by Lluís Domènech i Montaner for a guided tour (10:00 AM, ~€22 pp). Marvel at the stained-glass skylight, sculpted columns, and ornate ceramic mosaics. Afterwards, walk through the Sant Pere neighbourhood and visit the nearby Mercat de Santa Caterina for a colourful mid-morning break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Passeig de Gràcia Modernisme Walk – Stroll along Barcelona's grandest boulevard to see the 'Block of Discord': Casa Batlló (exterior or interior visit, ~€35 for standard entry), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Continue to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) for a rooftop visit (~€28) with its iconic chimneys and city views. This is one of the best ways to appreciate Gaudí's genius beyond the Sagrada Família.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – Return to the Palau for an evening concert (check programme at palaumusica.cat; tickets ~€30–60 depending on performance). Experiencing the hall illuminated at night with its full stained-glass splendour is unforgettable. Afterwards, enjoy a late dinner in the El Born or Eixample neighbourhood.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in Sant Antoni or similar specialty coffee spot in Eixample (~€8–12 for coffee and avocado toast).
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca – beloved local spot for tapas and montaditos, always buzzing. Budget ~€20–25 pp.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda or Parking Pizza in Eixample for a relaxed post-concert dinner. Budget ~€20–28 pp.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Palau evening concert well in advance – August performances sell out quickly. Casa Batlló and La Pedrera also benefit from advance booking. The afternoon walk along Passeig de Gràcia is best done after 17:00 when the heat eases slightly.

day_by_day.morning: Barceloneta Beach & Port Olímpic – Take the metro L4 to Barceloneta (~30 min). Spend the morning at the beach for a swim and relaxation before the heat peaks. Walk along the Passeig Marítim and admire Frank Gehry's golden 'Peix' (Fish) sculpture at Port Olímpic. Explore the Barceloneta neighbourhood's narrow streets and pick up fresh produce at the Mercat de la Barceloneta.
day_by_day.afternoon: El Raval & MACBA Area – Head to El Raval via metro or a 20-min walk. Visit the Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona (MACBA, ~€12) and admire Richard Meier's striking white building. Browse the surrounding streets for street art, vintage shops, and the bohemian atmosphere of this multicultural neighbourhood. Stop at the Filmoteca de Catalunya square for a rest.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and final Barcelona nightlife experience – Head to Eixample's 'Gayxample' area or Rambla del Poblenou for a final evening out. Enjoy a rooftop cocktail at Hotel Arts or the W Barcelona for sunset views over the Mediterranean, then a proper sit-down farewell dinner in Eixample before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, opens early) – legendary local bar, birthplace of the bombas tapa. Coffee and pastry ~€5.
meals.lunch: La Mar Salada near Barceloneta – fresh seafood with a sea view. Try the arrós negre (black rice). Budget ~€28–35 pp for a special lunch.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza or Bodega 1900 (Albert Adrià's vermouth bar-restaurant) in Sant Antoni for a memorable final dinner. Budget ~€30–40 pp.

day_by_day.notes: Check out logistics: if flying home on the 21st, confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange airport transfer. Barceloneta beach is very crowded in August – arrive before 10:00 AM for a good spot. Keep valuables secure in the beach area. The rooftop bar at W Barcelona requires smart-casual dress.

meals.dinner: Late dinner at Restaurante El Celler de Can Roca's sister concept or, closer to the hotel, Via Veneto (Carrer de Ganduxer) – a Michelin-starred Barcelona institution serving refined Catalan cuisine. Reserve in advance. Alternatively, enjoy the hotel's own restaurant for a relaxed first-night meal.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm private airport transfer before departure. August evenings in Barcelona are warm (~24°C), so light clothing is ideal. Tip: ask the hotel concierge to pre-book all restaurant reservations and experience tickets for the week upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Begin the day with a premium skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the August crowds. A private guide will decode the intricate symbolism of the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like nave, and the towers. Upgrade to include tower access via lift for panoramic city views. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk – After a leisurely lunch, join a small-group or private walking tour through Barcelona's medieval Gothic Quarter. Explore the Roman ruins beneath Plaça del Rei, the Cathedral of Barcelona, and transition into the trendy El Born neighbourhood to admire its 19th-century iron market (El Born Cultural Centre) and modernista streetscapes. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – Dress elegantly for a live concert at this breathtaking UNESCO World Heritage modernista masterpiece designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The stained-glass skylight and sculpted stage come alive under performance lighting. Check the August programme for classical or flamenco performances. Pre-book premium seats in the central stalls.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast at the hotel or head to Federal Café (El Born) for artisan coffee and avocado toast before the Sagrada Família tour.
meals.lunch: Alkimia (Ronda de Sant Antoni) – One Michelin star, avant-garde Catalan cuisine in a sleek setting. Alternatively, Bodega Sepúlveda for refined tapas near Eixample.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Llamber (El Born) – creative Mediterranean small plates in a sophisticated bistro atmosphere, a short walk from Palau de la Música.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets well in advance – August is peak season and slots sell out weeks ahead. The Gothic Quarter walk is best done in the afternoon when the light is golden and temperatures begin to ease. Wear comfortable but smart shoes for cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Pavillon Mies van der Rohe & Montjuïc Architecture Trail – Start at 10:00 AM with a visit to the iconic Barcelona Pavilion, the minimalist 1929 World Exposition masterpiece by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, featuring travertine marble, onyx walls, and the famous Barcelona Chair. Continue along the Montjuïc architecture trail, taking in the Fundació Joan Miró (designed by Josep Lluís Sert), the Palau Nacional (now MNAC), and the Olympic Ring complex. Hire a private architecture guide for deeper context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and recharge at the hotel pool or book a premium spa treatment. Alternatively, explore the upscale Passeig de Gràcia boulevard – visit Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) with priority access tickets, two more Gaudí masterpieces that complement the morning's modernista theme. The 'Block of Discord' on Passeig de Gràcia also features Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera.
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec & Montjuïc Nightlife Circuit – Experience Barcelona's vibrant nightlife starting with pintxos and vermouth at a top Poble Sec bar (Carrer de Blai, the 'pintxos street'). Move on to a cocktail at a rooftop terrace with Montjuïc views, then head to Sala Apolo or Paral·lel theatre district for live music or a show. End the night at a sophisticated cocktail lounge in the Eixample.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Forn de Sant Jaume (Passeig de Gràcia) for premium pastries and coffee.
meals.lunch: Quimet & Quimet (Poble Sec) – legendary standing tapas bar famous for creative montaditos and tinned seafood, a Barcelona institution. Arrive early as it fills quickly.
meals.dinner: Tickets (Avinguda del Paral·lel) – Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas restaurant, one of Barcelona's most celebrated dining experiences. Book months in advance. Alternatively, Bodega 1900 (same group) for a more relaxed vermouth-bar concept.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc can be reached by cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) from Paral·lel metro station for a scenic ascent. August heat peaks around 29°C – plan outdoor architecture walks for morning or late afternoon. Tickets restaurant requires reservations made months ahead; confirm before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private Eixample Modernisme Deep Dive – Dedicate the morning to Barcelona's Eixample district, the grid-planned 19th-century expansion that became the canvas for Catalan Modernisme. With a private architect guide, explore the facades of Domènech i Montaner's Hospital de Sant Pau (a UNESCO site), Puig i Cadafalch's Casa Amatller, and lesser-known modernista gems. Visit the interior of Casa Milà (La Pedrera) including the rooftop terrace with its surreal chimneys and the Espai Gaudí exhibition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta & Port Olímpic Coastal Afternoon – Take a taxi or private transfer to the waterfront. Stroll along the Barceloneta promenade, visit Frank Gehry's shimmering 'Fish' sculpture at Port Olímpic, and relax at a premium beach club (Boca Grande or W Barcelona's Eclipse Bar terrace). Enjoy the Mediterranean breeze and a refreshing swim.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop Cocktails & Upscale Nightlife in Eixample – Begin the evening at the rooftop bar of the Hotel Arts or W Barcelona for sunset cocktails with panoramic sea views. Transition to the Eixample 'Gayxample' district for dinner, then explore Barcelona's sophisticated cocktail bar scene: Paradiso (El Born) – a speakeasy behind a pastrami bar, consistently ranked among the world's best bars – is a must-visit. End the night at a jazz club or a late-night lounge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Brunch & Cake (Eixample) for a healthy, Instagram-worthy brunch spread.
meals.lunch: La Mar Salada (near Barceloneta) – refined seafood restaurant with a terrace, celebrated for its paella and fresh Mediterranean catch.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar (Carrer de Villarroel) – two Michelin stars, ranked among the world's top restaurants, run by former elBulli chefs. An unmissable avant-garde tasting menu experience. Book 2–3 months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Disfrutar is arguably the most important reservation of the trip – confirm well before travel. The beach clubs along Barceloneta can be crowded in August; consider booking a sunbed or VIP area in advance. Paradiso bar opens at 18:00 and queues form quickly – arrive early or check if reservations are available.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell & Upper Barcelona – Begin with a private or small-group tour of Park Güell, Gaudí's fantastical hilltop park with its mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and sweeping city panoramas. Book the timed-entry Monumental Zone tickets in advance. Afterwards, explore the Gràcia neighbourhood below – a charming village-within-the-city with independent boutiques, café terraces, and modernista architecture including Casa Vicens (Gaudí's first major work).
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Shopping & Spa – Spend the afternoon on Passeig de Gràcia and Avinguda Diagonal for high-end shopping (Loewe, Hermès, local designer boutiques). Alternatively, book a premium spa session at the Mandarin Oriental Barcelona or the Grand Hotel Central for a restorative afternoon before the final evening. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Final Barcelona Night – Celebrate the last evening with a memorable dinner at a top Barcelona restaurant. Afterwards, take a final evening walk along Las Ramblas and through the Gothic Quarter, stopping for a nightcap at El Xampanyet (El Born) for cava, or head to a rooftop bar for one last view of the illuminated Barcelona skyline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – take your time on the final morning.
meals.lunch: Bar Calders (Sant Antoni neighbourhood) – beloved local spot for vermouth, anchovies, and pintxos in a relaxed, authentic atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Lasarte (Hotel Monument, Passeig de Gràcia) – three Michelin stars, helmed by Martín Berasategui, offering an extraordinary Basque-Catalan haute cuisine tasting menu in an elegant setting. A perfect farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed-entry tickets must be booked online in advance – August slots sell out days ahead. If departing the following morning, arrange a private transfer the night before. Keep the final evening flexible to allow for spontaneous exploration of whichever neighbourhood has captured your heart during the week. Average August rainfall is moderate (47.5 mm/month) – carry a compact umbrella just in case of a brief afternoon shower.
